mainTopic: שבועת העדות: counting liabilities for a multi-part denial, and whether witnesses to a קנס are liable
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about two sets of witnesses: רבינא explains that the first set is liable because the second set could not testify at that moment, since they were relatives through wives who were גוססות but still alive. Then a new משנה teaches that when witnesses deny a claim with several parts, their own wording decides the count. A general denial means one liability, and naming each item means a liability for each one. The משנה also lists claims such as נזק, חצי נזק, כפל, ארבעה וחמשה, אונס ומפתה, injuries, and burning a grain stack on יום הכפורים, and makes witnesses who deny them liable. The גמרא asks whether witnesses to a קנס are liable, and shows that the question exists only for the רבנן, who say admitting exempts from a fine and that דבר הגורם לממון is not money. It tries to prove the answer from each case in the משנה, but each case is explained as ממון: חצי נזק as money or as צרורות, כפל and ארבעה וחמשה because of the קרן, and אונס ומפתה because of בושת and פגם. The long list is then justified: the רישא teaches that חצי נזק צרורות is money, and the סיפא rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה about damage done on יום הכפורים. At the end, the גמרא begins a new proof from a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But the second set of witnesses is still available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the first set of witnesses is liable, because a second set could still testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the second set of witnesses is still standing there, ready to testify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question on the earlier ruling that the first set of witnesses is liable for denying testimony. If a second set could still testify, the first set's denial didn't really cause the claimant any loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבועת העדות makes witnesses liable when their refusal to testify causes a loss. Here the claimant still had another pair of witnesses available, so the first pair's denial seems harmless. That would mean they should not be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: stands, is still available
the second set of witnesses
a set or group of witnesses (here understood)

phrases.english: But the second set still stands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier ruling (from before this section) that the first set of witnesses is liable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the first set of witnesses is liable even though a second set existed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability for denying testimony requires causing a loss. A second, available set means no loss was caused.

steps.title: The second set was disqualified as relatives at that moment
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the second pair of witnesses were related to each other through their wives when the first pair denied, so only the first pair could testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: What case are we dealing with? A case where, at the time the first set denied, the two witnesses of the second set were related through their wives, and their wives were dying. You might think: most dying people do die, so treat them as already dead. The משנה teaches us: right now, at least, the wives have not died.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains the earlier ruling with a specific case: the second set was disqualified at the time the first set denied. So the first set was the claimant's only real hope, and their denial did cause a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two witnesses of the second set were married to sisters, which makes them relatives who cannot testify together. Even though their wives were גוססות and would most likely die soon, the law looks at the present moment: they are still alive. So at the time of the first denial the second set could not testify, and the first set is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here?
related through their wives
dying, in their final moments
most dying people end up dying
you might have thought / so it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second set is disqualified forever. They are disqualified only right now, because their wives are still alive. Once the wives die they could testify, but what counts is the moment the first set denied.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גוסס is treated as alive for הלכה, even though most גוססים die. We go by the present situation, not by what will probably happen.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where the second set was,
at the time of the first set's denial,
relatives through their wives,
phrases.notes: The two witnesses were married to two sisters, so they count as relatives and can't testify together.

phrases.english: and their wives were dying.
You might have said:
most dying people go on to die,
phrases.notes: So you might treat the wives as already dead, and the husbands as no longer related.

phrases.english: so it teaches us:
now, at least, she has not died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the case so that the second set was not actually available.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): a specific situation where the second set was disqualified.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most dying people die, the wives could be treated as dead, making the second set valid witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוסס is still alive now, so the second set was disqualified at the time of the first denial, and the first set is liable.

steps.title: A general denial of a multi-part claim makes them liable only once
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that if witnesses answer a claim with several parts with one general oath, they are liable for only one oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The claimant says: "I make you swear, if you do not come and testify for me that so-and-so holds my deposit, my loan, a stolen item and a lost item." They answer: "We swear that we do not know any testimony for you." They are liable for only one oath.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. A claimant asks witnesses to testify about four separate things, and they deny with one general oath that they know no testimony for him; they are liable only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the claim had four parts, the witnesses' oath was one general statement: "we know no testimony." Since they did not mention each item, it counts as a single false oath, so they bring only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: the משנה
I make you take an oath
a deposit left with someone
a loan or money handed over (literally, putting into the hand)
a stolen item and a lost item

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"I make you swear,
if you do not come and testify for me
that I have in the hands of so-and-so
a deposit and a loan
and a stolen item and a lost item";
"We swear that we do not know testimony for you"–
they are liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַשְׁבִּיעַ אֲנִי עֲלֵיכֶם, אִם לֹא תָבוֹאוּ וּתְעִידוּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about counting how many oaths the witnesses are liable for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single general denial of a multi-part claim makes the witnesses liable for only one oath.

steps.title: Denying each item by name makes them liable for each one
steps.stepSummary: If the witnesses list each item in their denial, they are liable separately for every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they answer: "We swear that we do not know that you have in the hands of so-and-so a deposit, a loan, a stolen item and a lost item," they are liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the contrasting case: the witnesses deny by naming each item. Now they are liable for every item separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is only in the wording of their oath. By naming each item, their oath is treated as several oaths, one for each thing they denied, so they owe a separate קרבן for each.

keyTerms.meaning: liable for each and every one
we swear that we do not know

steps.whatToRemember: The number of oaths follows the witnesses' own wording: a general denial ("we know no testimony") counts as one; naming each item counts as one for each item.

phrases.english: "We swear that we do not know
that you have in the hands of so-and-so
a deposit and a loan
and a stolen item and a lost item"–
they are liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְךָ בְּיַד פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to the previous step: a specific, item-by-item denial instead of a general one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A denial that names each item makes the witnesses liable for a separate oath on every item.

steps.title: A deposit of several grains with one general denial
steps.stepSummary: The claimant asks the witnesses to testify about a deposit of wheat, barley and spelt. If they deny with one general oath, they are liable for only one שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, "I make you swear: come and testify that so-and-so is holding a deposit of wheat, barley and spelt for me," and they answer, "We swear we know no testimony for you," they are liable for only one oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new example of the rule from step 3: a claim about three kinds of grain, answered with one general denial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim has three parts, but the witnesses' oath never mentions any of them. Because they swore only once, in general terms, they bring only one קרבן שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit, something left with another person to look after
Wheat, barley and spelt
The oath of testimony: witnesses swear falsely that they know nothing
They are liable for only one oath

phrases.english: "I administer an oath to you,
if you do not come and testify
that I have in the possession of so-and-so
a deposit of wheat, and barley, and spelt";
and they answer: "An oath that we do not know any testimony for you"
they are liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁבִּיעַ אֲנִי עֲלֵיכֶם, אִם לֹא תָבוֹאוּ וְתָעִידוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general-denial rule from step 3 to a claim about several kinds of grain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A general denial of a claim about several items makes the witnesses liable for one oath only.

steps.title: The same grain claim with each item named in the denial
steps.stepSummary: If the witnesses name the wheat, barley and spelt in their false oath, they are liable for each item separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they answer, "We swear we know no testimony for you that so-and-so has your wheat, barley and spelt," they are liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the grain case: the witnesses name each item in their denial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from step 5 is the wording of the witnesses' oath. Naming every item counts as a separate denial for each one, so each item brings its own liability, the same rule as step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable for each and every one
So-and-so, an unnamed person

steps.confusionAlert: The claim is identical in steps 5 and 6. What changes the ruling is whether the witnesses' own oath mentions each item.

phrases.english: "An oath that we do not know any testimony for you
that you have in the possession of so-and-so
wheat, and barley, and spelt"
they are liable for each and every one.

steps.whatToRemember: One general denial means one liability. A denial that names each item means a separate liability for each item.
steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין לְךָ עֵדוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְךָ בְּיַד פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting half of step 5, matching the itemized-denial rule of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming each item in the false denial makes the witnesses liable for each item separately.

steps.title: Witnesses denying claims of damages, special payments and injuries are liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists claims such as damage, half-damage, double payment, four and five payments, rape, seduction, a son striking his father, injury, and burning a grain stack on יום הכפורים. Witnesses who falsely deny knowing about any of these are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, "I make you swear: come and testify for me that so-and-so owes me for damage, half-damage, double payment, or four and five payment, or that he raped or seduced my daughter, or my son hit me, or my friend injured me, or he burned my grain stack on יום הכפורים," then these witnesses are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists many kinds of claims and rules that witnesses who falsely deny them are liable for שבועת העדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of these payments are more than plain repayment of a loss, such as כפל and ארבעה וחמשה. The list even includes acts that carry a severe punishment, like a son striking his father or burning on יום הכפורים. Even so, the משנה rules that these witnesses are liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Half-damage, paid for damage done by an ox not known to gore
Double payment that a thief pays
Four or five times the value, paid for a stolen sheep or ox that was slaughtered or sold
Raped / seduced
Injured
A stack of grain

steps.whyThisMatters: This list prepares the גמרא's question in step 8 about witnesses to a קנס, a fixed penalty payment.

phrases.english: "I administer an oath to you,
if you do not come and testify for me
that I have in the possession of so-and-so
payment for damage, or half the damage,
or double payment,
or payment of four or five times,
phrases.notes: Four times the value for a sheep, five for an ox, when the thief slaughtered or sold it.

phrases.english: or that so-and-so raped my daughter,
or seduced my daughter,
or that my son struck me,
or that another person injured me,
or that he set my grain stack on fire on Yom Kippur"
these witnesses are liable.

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses who falsely deny knowledge of all these claims are liable for שבועת העדות.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁבִּיעַ אֲנִי עֲלֵיכֶם, אִם לֹא תָבוֹאוּ וּתְעִידוּנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּיַד פְּלוֹנִי נֶזֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how many oaths the witnesses owe to which kinds of claims make them liable at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who falsely deny knowing about damages, special payments, injuries and the other listed claims are liable.

steps.title: Are witnesses to a fine liable for שבועת העדות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when someone makes witnesses swear about a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: if someone makes witnesses to a קנס swear, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with an open question about witnesses whose testimony would make someone pay a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a fixed penalty set by the תורה, not repayment for a loss. The question is whether such a claim counts as a money claim for שבועת העדות, so that witnesses who falsely deny it are liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
They asked a question (an unresolved question was raised)
A fine: a fixed penalty set by the תורה
What is the law?

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
One who administers an oath to witnesses of a fine, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַשְׁבִּיעַ עֵדֵי קְנָס, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion, building on the משנה's list of claims in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether witnesses who falsely deny knowing about a קנס are liable for שבועת העדות, like witnesses to an ordinary money claim.

steps.title: No question according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the question about a קנס does not arise, because he holds that witnesses can still come and testify even after the person admits.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, you have no question, because he says: let the witnesses come and testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing the question from step 8. It says that for one opinion, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person who admits to a קנס is exempt from paying it. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that if there were witnesses, they can still come and testify, and he pays the fine. So the fine really depends on the witnesses. That makes their testimony a money matter, and a false denial makes them liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine, a payment set by the תורה beyond the actual damage (like double payment)
According to the opinion of
You don't need to ask; there is no question here
Let the witnesses come and testify

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'let the witnesses come and testify' come from a different place where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון rules about someone who admitted to a קנס before witnesses came. They are not a new rule invented here.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon –
you should not ask the question,
for he says: let the witnesses come and testify.
phrases.notes: He means: even after the person admitted to the fine, witnesses can still testify and make him pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 8 by ruling out one opinion where it doesn't arise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, witnesses denying a קנס are clearly liable, since the fine depends on their testimony even after an admission.

steps.title: The question arises according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The question only arises according to the רבנן, who hold that one who admits to a קנס is exempt even if witnesses come afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do you have a question? According to the רבנן, who say: if someone admits to a קנס and afterward witnesses came, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says exactly where the question in step 8 belongs: according to the רבנן who argue with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, once the person admits, the witnesses can no longer make him pay. So the fine does not fully depend on the witnesses, because the defendant could make himself exempt just by admitting. That makes it unclear whether their testimony counts as a money matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Where you should ask the question
One who admits that he owes a fine
Exempt

phrases.english: Where you should ask –
is according to the Rabbis, who say:
one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came – is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the narrowing begun in step 9 by naming the opinion where the question applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, admitting to a קנס exempts a person even if witnesses come later, so the question arises only by them.

steps.title: Which view do those רבנן hold about 'something that causes money'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom the רבנן of the קנס case agree with. If they agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון of our סוגיא, who says דבר הגורם לממון counts as money, there would be no question at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן of there, whose view do they follow? If you say they follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון of here, he says that something that causes money counts as money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the question can still stand. It asks which opinion the רבנן of the קנס case hold about testimony that only leads to money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in this סוגיא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said that testimony which causes money to be paid counts as money. If the רבנן of the קנס case agreed with him, testimony about a fine would surely count, because it causes payment, and there would be nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן of there (the case about admitting to a fine)
Whose opinion do they hold?
If you say
Something that causes money to be paid is treated like money

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different arguments involving רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: one 'there' about admitting to a קנס, and one 'here' in our סוגיא about something that causes money. Keep 'there' and 'here' apart.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis of there,
phrases.notes: These are the רבנן from step 10, who say admitting to a fine exempts you.

phrases.english: whose view do they hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּהָכָא,
phrases.english: If you say like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon of here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means earlier in our own סוגיא, back on 32a.

phrases.english: but he says:
a thing that causes money is like money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the question placed in step 10 can really stand.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן of the קנס case hold that דבר הגורם לממון counts as money? If they do, the question would be answered right away.

steps.title: They must hold like the רבנן of our סוגיא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of the קנס case must agree with the רבנן of our סוגיא, who hold that something that only causes money does not count as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they follow the רבנן of here, who say: something that causes money is not treated like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own check. The question stands only for someone who holds that דבר הגורם לממון is not money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, testimony counts only if it is directly about money. A fine is in between: the witnesses do make him pay, but he could avoid paying by admitting. That is why the question is real.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן of here (our סוגיא)
Is not treated like money

phrases.english: Rather, like the Rabbis of here, who say:
a thing that causes money
is not like money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the check in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן of the קנס case hold like the רבנן of our sugya: דבר הגורם לממון is not treated as money.

steps.title: The question stated clearly: is denying a fine denying money?
steps.stepSummary: The question is stated in full. Since admitting would exempt him, maybe the witness isn't denying money. Or maybe, since he hasn't admitted yet, the fine still depends on the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since if he admitted he would be exempt, the witness is not denying him money? Or perhaps, right now at least, he has not admitted?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא knows whose opinion it is working with, it states the question with its two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the defendant could cancel the fine at any time by admitting, so the witnesses' testimony is not truly about money, and they would be exempt. Side two: right now he has not admitted, so at this moment the payment depends on the witnesses, and their denial is a denial of money.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?
Since
He becomes exempt
Denied
Or perhaps
Now, at least

steps.whatToRemember: The question is only according to the רבנן, who hold that admitting exempts from a קנס and that דבר הגורם לממון is not money. Is the witness not denying money, since admitting would cancel the fine? Or is he denying money, since right now the defendant hasn't admitted?
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: something that could be cancelled later, versus how things stand right now.

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since if he would admit he would be exempt –
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the one who owes the fine, not the witness.

phrases.english: it is not money that he is denying him;
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is the witness, and 'him' is the person claiming the fine.

phrases.english: or perhaps,
now, at least, he has not admitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of step 8, now stated in full according to the opinion set in steps 10 and 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a witness who falsely denies knowing about a קנס liable for שבועת העדות, given that the defendant could have exempted himself by admitting, but has not admitted yet?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's case of half-damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where witnesses are made to swear about נזק and חצי נזק. Since חצי נזק is a קנס, this would seem to show that witnesses are liable even about a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I make you swear: if you do not come and testify for me that so-and-so owes me damage and half-damage.' But half-damage is a fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 13 using our own משנה. The משנה makes witnesses liable when they deny knowing about חצי נזק, and חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses are liable for denying testimony about חצי נזק, and חצי נזק is a fine, then a fine counts as 'money' for שבועת העדות. That would settle the question: the witness is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear: the wording of the oath put on the witnesses
Half-damage: what an owner pays when his ox gores before it is known as a goring ox
A fine: a payment that is not simply covering a loss

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"I make you swear,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our own משנה about שבועת העדות.

phrases.english: if you do not come and testify for me
that I have in the hand of so-and-so
damage and half-damage."
But half-damage is a fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the question asked in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Witnesses are liable for שבועת העדות about a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists חצי נזק among the cases where witnesses are liable.

steps.title: The משנה follows the view that half-damage is money
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The משנה follows the opinion that חצי נזק is ordinary money and not a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows the one who says half-damage is money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof. There is an opinion that חצי נזק is ממון, and the משנה may follow that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known disagreement about whether חצי נזק is a fine or real money. If the משנה follows the 'money' opinion, it tells us nothing about a real קנס, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the one who says: this source matches a particular opinion
Half-damage is money: the opinion that it is real payment for a loss

phrases.english: It follows the one who says
half-damage is money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only according to one opinion about חצי נזק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed חצי נזק is a קנס, but the משנה may hold it is ממון.

steps.title: What about the view that half-damage is a fine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses: that answer works for the 'money' opinion, but how does the other opinion, which calls חצי נזק a fine, explain the משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says half-damage is money. But for the one who says it is a fine, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection. The other opinion still has to explain why the משנה makes witnesses liable about חצי נזק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the 'fine' opinion, the משנה really does seem to make witnesses liable about a קנס. So for that opinion the proof is still standing.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well: it fits one opinion, but now comes a problem
What can be said? This asks how the other opinion would explain it

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
half-damage is money;
but for the one who says it is a fine,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּלְגָא נִזְקָא מָמוֹנָא אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קְנָסָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 15 because it only works for one opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer only covers one opinion. For the opinion that חצי נזק is a קנס, the משנה still seems to prove liability about a fine.

steps.title: The משנה means half-damage of pebbles
steps.stepSummary: Even the 'fine' opinion can explain the משנה. It is talking about חצי נזק צרורות, which a הלכה למשה מסיני teaches is money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about half-damage from pebbles, which they learned by tradition is money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's חצי נזק is the special case of צרורות. Everyone agrees that case is ממון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal kicks up pebbles while walking and they cause damage, the owner pays half. A tradition teaches this half is real money, not a fine. So even the 'fine' opinion can read the משנה this way, and the proof about a real קנס falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks, which cause damage
They learned it as a tradition: a הלכה למשה מסיני

steps.confusionAlert: Not every חצי נזק is the same. The 'fine' opinion is about a תם ox that gores. The half-damage for צרורות is money according to everyone.

phrases.english: It is about half-damage of pebbles,
which they learned as a tradition
that it is money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific situation (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's חצי נזק is the fine-type half-damage of a goring ox.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about צרורות, which is money by tradition, so it proves nothing about a קנס.

steps.title: Proof from double payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again from the משנה: witnesses are liable for denying testimony about תשלומי כפל, which is a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'double payment'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case from the same משנה. Witnesses are liable even about תשלומי כפל, the double payment a thief pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra amount in כפל is clearly a קנס. If witnesses are liable for denying testimony about it, then a fine counts for שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment: a thief pays back twice what he stole

phrases.english: Come and hear: "double payment"!
phrases.notes: Same משנה: "testify that so-and-so owes me double payment." The extra half is a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof attempt after the first one was turned away.
steps.raayaObject: Witnesses are liable for שבועת העדות about a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of תשלומי כפל.

steps.title: Liable because of the principal
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses are liable because of the קרן, the basic stolen amount, not because of the fine part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. Their testimony would also prove the basic amount owed, and that amount is real money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses denied testimony about the whole payment, which includes the קרן. The liability can come from the קרן alone, so we still cannot tell what the law is for the fine part.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal: the basic amount stolen, which is ordinary money
Because of

phrases.english: Because of the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The liability can be explained by the קרן, which is money, so the case says nothing about the fine.

steps.title: Proof from four and five payment
steps.stepSummary: Another try from the משנה: witnesses are liable about תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה, which is a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And payment of four and five'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last case in the משנה: the four- or fivefold payment of a thief who slaughtered or sold the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying four or five times the value is mostly a קנס. The משנה makes the witnesses liable here too, so the גמרא tries to prove from it that fines count.

keyTerms.meaning: Four or five times the value, paid by a thief who slaughtered or sold a stolen sheep or ox

phrases.english: "And payment of four and five"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another proof attempt from the same משנה, following the rejection in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: Witnesses are liable for שבועת העדות about a קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Again, liable because of the principal
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: the liability comes from the קרן included in the payment, not from the fine. The question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way. The witnesses' testimony also covers the basic amount, which is money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the four or five payments is the original value of the animal, which is real money. That part alone is enough to make the witnesses liable, so the משנה does not prove anything about a pure קנס.
steps.whatToRemember: So far none of the משנה's cases settle the question. חצי נזק can be explained as money (one opinion, or צרורות), and כפל and ארבעה וחמשה make witnesses liable because of the קרן. The next step tries one more case from the משנה, אונס ומפתה.

phrases.english: Because of the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20 using the same reasoning as step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ארבעה וחמשה proof completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The liability is explained by the קרן inside the payment, not by the fine.

steps.title: A proof from the rape and seduction case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again from the משנה. Witnesses are liable for denying testimony that someone raped or seduced the man's daughter, and those cases carry a fixed fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says witnesses are liable if they deny knowing 'that so-and-so raped or seduced my daughter.' That payment is a fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the משנה to prove that witnesses are liable even about a קנס. The rapist and the seducer pay a fixed 50 סלעים, which is a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed payment of 50 סלעים for אונס and מפתה is a classic קנס. If the משנה makes witnesses liable here, that seems to prove the oath of testimony applies to fines too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rapes a young woman; he pays a fixed fine of 50 סלעים
One who seduces a young woman; he also pays the fixed fine
A fine: a fixed payment set by the תורה, not tied to actual loss

phrases.english: "That so-and-so raped
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, the words the plaintiff uses when he makes the witnesses swear.

phrases.english: or seduced my daughter"! (That is a fine!)
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the punchline unsaid: the 50 סלעים payment is a fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאָנַס אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי וּפִתָּה אֶת בִּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another attempt from the משנה, after חצי נזק (step 14), כפל (step 18) and ארבעה וחמשה (step 20)
steps.raayaObject: That שבועת העדות applies to testimony about a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of אונס ומפתה, which carries a fixed fine of 50 סלעים

steps.title: Liable because of humiliation and degradation
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The witnesses are liable because of the payments for בושת and פגם, which are normal money payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: No proof: the liability is because of the payments for humiliation and degradation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the witnesses are not liable because of the fine. They are liable because of other payments the man must make, for shame and for lowering her value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the fine, the אונס and מפתה also pay בושת and פגם, and these are regular compensation (ממון). Those payments alone are enough to make the witnesses liable, so nothing is proven about fines. This follows the same pattern as steps 19 and 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment for humiliation
Payment for degradation, meaning the drop in her value

phrases.english: It is because of humiliation and degradation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from אונס ומפתה; the main question stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case also involves money payments (בושת and פגם), so the liability can come from them and not from the fine

steps.title: Why list so many cases?
steps.stepSummary: If every case in the משנה is really about money, what is the משנה teaching by listing so many cases?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the משנה teaching us? It is all just money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the approach it has been using. If every case comes down to regular money, the long list in the משנה seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each proof was pushed away by saying 'the liability comes from the money part.' But then all the cases teach the same simple rule, that witnesses are liable for money. So why does the משנה repeat it again and again?

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? Asked when a ruling seems to add nothing new
Money: regular compensation, as opposed to a fine

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
All of it is money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the overall result of the rejections in steps 17 through 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that every case in the משנה is about ממון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every case teaches the same rule, the repeated cases are unnecessary

steps.title: The first part teaches that pebble damage is money
steps.stepSummary: The רישא and the סיפא each teach one new point. The רישא teaches that חצי נזק צרורות counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part teaches one thing and the last part teaches one thing. The first part teaches that half-damage for pebbles is money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not repeating itself. Each part has its own new lesson, and the first lesson is about חצי נזק צרורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the משנה, one might think חצי נזק צרורות is a fine, since it is only half the damage. The רישא teaches that it is ממון, so witnesses who deny knowing about it are liable. This ties back to step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
Half-damage paid when an animal kicks up pebbles that cause damage

phrases.english: The first part teaches us one thing,
the last part teaches us one thing;
the first part teaches us one thing:
that half-damage for pebbles is money.
phrases.notes: This is the הלכה למשה מסיני mentioned back in step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each clause has its own separate new lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since it is only half, חצי נזק צרורות might have been a fine
steps.terutzMaskana: חצי נזק צרורות is ממון, so the רישא teaches something new

steps.title: The last part: burning grain on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא teaches a separate new point. Someone who burned a stack of grain on יום הכפורים still has to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part teaches one thing: 'that he burned my stack of grain on יום הכפורים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by naming the new lesson in the סיפא: the case of burning grain on יום הכפורים. It is setting up the question of what view this case is meant to reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה makes witnesses liable here, it must hold that the damager pays even though he burned the grain on יום הכפורים. Doing a forbidden act on that day does not free him from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: A stack of harvested grain
The Day of Atonement, when work is forbidden under the penalty of כרת

phrases.english: The last part teaches us one thing:
"And that he set my grain stack on fire
on יום הכפורים."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer begun in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the separate new lesson of the סיפא
steps.terutzMaskana: Damage done on יום הכפורים still must be paid

steps.title: Which view does this reject?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion the יום הכפורים case is meant to reject.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it coming to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who would have thought otherwise. It is setting up the next step, which names that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new lesson only matters if someone might have disagreed. The גמרא wants to know who would exempt a person who damaged on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject a different view

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the lesson given in step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion would exempt a person who damaged on יום הכפורים

steps.title: Rejecting רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who treated יום הכפורים like שבת and exempted damage done while sinning on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. A ברייתא teaches that he treated יום הכפורים like שבת for payments: just as on שבת and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the rejected view. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה held that a person who damages while doing a forbidden act on יום הכפורים does not pay, just as on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person who deserves death for his act is exempt from paying for damage he did at the same time. רבי נחוניא applied this to יום הכפורים, whose penalty is כרת. The משנה makes the witnesses liable, so it holds that the damager does pay, against רבי נחוניא.

keyTerms.meaning: Payments for damage

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נחוניא is not saying the damage is fine to do. He is saying the worse punishment for the sin cancels the duty to pay money, the way it does on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Every case in the משנה is ממון. The רישא teaches that חצי נזק צרורות is money, and the סיפא teaches that damage done on יום הכפורים must be paid, against רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה,
as it is taught:
רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
would treat יום הכפורים
like שבת regarding payments,
just as שבת, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא shortens a line we already know: just as one who sins on שבת is exempt from paying, so too on יום הכפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who exempted damage done while sinning on יום הכפורים
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the reading that every case in the משנה is ממון, so the משנה does not settle the question about fines. In step 29 the גמרא turns to a ברייתא instead.

steps.title: A new proof from a ברייתא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the question, this time from a ברייתא about a man who makes witnesses swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I make you swear: if you do not come and testify for me...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to settle whether the oath of testimony applies to a fine. The quote continues on the next amud, so this line is only setting up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs from the משנה have all been pushed away, so the גמרא turns to a different source. The key case inside the ברייתא has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear: the wording used to put witnesses under oath

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"I make you swear,
if you do not come and testify for me

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the משנה fail, a new proof from a ברייתא begins
steps.raayaObject: Whether שבועת העדות applies to a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא; the quote continues past this point
